title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI quality gating and metrics integration
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Adds a per-prompt prompt-set regression and quality gating step to eval-harness CI. This introduces per-prompt metric computation, threshold-based gating, and a lightweight GitHub Actions hook that reports metrics and fails the PR when any prompt drops below configured thresholds. Motivation: several incidents showed regressions that only affected a small subset of prompts. Global aggregate metrics passed CI while important prompts regressed in production. This change surfaces per-prompt regressions in developer CI to prevent silent breakages and to provide structured metrics for triage.  What this PR does: 1) Implements a per-prompt metrics exporter in eval-harness that emits JSON reports for per-prompt scores (accuracy, pass_rate, rouge, etc.). 2) Adds a new GH Actions job (eval/per-prompt-gate) that downloads the report artifact, compares against a configurable baseline and per-prompt thresholds stored in eval/config/prompt_thresholds.yaml, and fails the job if any prompt falls below its threshold or if median regression exceeds a relative tolerance. 3) Integrates with CI annotations so failing prompts surface as check annotations with links to examples. 4) Adds a small metrics integration that posts summarized per-prompt deltas to our internal metrics endpoint and attaches a summary in the PR comment. 5) Adds docs and test vectors for the gating logic.  Backward compatibility and config: The gating is opt-in per-repository via eval-harness/.github/workflows/eval-per-prompt-gate.yml. Default behavior for existing repos is unchanged (disabled) until the workflow is enabled. Thresholds have sensible defaults and can be overridden by teams.  Risk and testing: Unit and integration tests added for the gating comparator. I ran the new workflow against a historical dataset (2026-01 monthly eval) and verified it caught two known regressions that previous CI missed. CI ran green after addressing an initial false-positive in the string normalization step.  Notes for reviewers: Focus on the gating comparator semantics (relative vs absolute thresholds), caching of baseline artifacts, and security review of the metrics poster. See commits for incremental changes.  Related: ENG-2147 implements internal alerting when per-prompt drift crosses operational thresholds. SUP-789 tracked a customer incident where a rare prompt regression affected a high-value flow.

review_threads: Ben Carlson: Could the comparator run into flakiness if we have very small sample sizes for a prompt? Suggest adding a minimum sample-size guard.  Asha: Added min_sample_size=30 with a fallback to skip gating and annotate as 'insufficient-data' in the CI summary.

Maya Singh: Do we need encryption or PII filtering before posting metric examples to internal endpoints?  Asha: Post only aggregate deltas and example IDs; we explicitly strip any raw user text. Added a filter and doc note.

Li Wei: The GH Actions job downloads baseline artifacts from the release bucket; what if the artifact is missing?  Asha: Fallback behavior added: job marks baseline-missing and skips gating but still posts metrics for manual triage.

integration: eval-harness integration tests - failed (initially due to prompt id normalization), rerun passed
release_notes: Add opt-in per-prompt CI gating to eval-harness. Provides early detection of prompt-specific regressions and integrates per-prompt metrics into PR CI. Default: disabled; teams must enable workflow. See docs for configuration.
additional_notes: Workflow is opt-in and scoped to repos that enable the eval-per-prompt-gate workflow. Operations should review the metrics poster endpoint before enabling in production-sensitive repos.
